- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and model forecast is below recent 10-day average, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with bullish sentiment.
- Model frequently overpredicts in early horizon (1–5 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; apply 1–2% downward bias for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., 0.00–0.27) after a peak, model often fails to correct; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.30.
- For 10+ day forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.53–0.80), model often averages out sentiment; use sentiment-weighted median or 3-period moving average to reduce noise.
